# Your own study: define the question

Use this route for compatible quantitative-trait beta summary statistics. Complete synthetic practice first, then use the GLGC example to see why source-method context matters.

::: {.callout-note icon=false}
## Write your question

“For [trait] in [documented study population], where are the strongest released variant associations, and what do their effects and uncertainty support?”
:::

Record the publication/accession, phenotype processing, study design, population descriptors, genome build, effect allele, effect units and source test. Decide whether the file is genome-wide or a selected list.

## Is this workflow suitable?

| Your input | Decision |
|---|---|
| Quantitative-trait beta, positive SE, autosomal SNVs and documented metadata | Prepare the contract and proceed |
| Odds ratios or log-odds | Extend the model and labels first; do not relabel them as quantitative beta |
| Genotypes and participant phenotypes | This guide starts later; use an appropriate genotype-QC/association pipeline |
| Selected variants only | Use descriptive plots; Q–Q and lambda will be skipped |
| Missing study definitions or unknown build | Resolve against the original source before interpretation |

A compatible table can still have unsuitable source assumptions. Do not use the finished synthetic or GLGC answers as findings for your study.
